Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so your security and procurement teams have a single source of truth. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of what we heard (pain / goals):
- Auditability: Acme needs searchable, tamper-evident audit logs for admin + API activity for the last 12+ months for compliance and investigations.
- Data residency & retention: primary requirement is US residency with the ability to set log retention to 12+ months for compliance.
- DPA & subprocessors: legal requires a DPA with a complete subprocessor list and standard liability language.
- Pen test evidence: security team needs a redacted pen test summary and remediation status (not full raw scans).
- Encryption & key management: confirmation of at-rest encryption and KMS/HSM integration for dedicated/private deployments.

What Redwood can share today (attachments below):
- Redacted SOC 2 Type II report (control coverage, test period summary)
- Pen test summary (redacted findings + remediation status)
- Our standard DPA template (we can negotiate narrow edits)

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and for sharing the artifacts. A few clarifying items from our side:

- Retention: our compliance team is asking for 13 months of immutable audit logs for admin/API events. Is that achievable on the hosted plan or only on dedicated/private deployments?
- DPA: please confirm the subprocessors list and whether you can accept our standard breach notification SLA (48 hours). Legal also wants to know if any subprocessors have access to decrypted customer data.
- Pen test: the summary is helpful; can we get a redacted appendix that includes affected endpoints and CVE identifiers (no raw logs or PII)?
- Encryption: confirm whether your hosted offering supports customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS or HSM. If not, what timeline is available to enable CMK for Enterprise customers?

Procurement note: Lauren (cc’d) needs an executed DPA and a ballpark for how long it takes to get the audit artifacts and an evidence package for our internal auditors.

If we can get answers to the above and the attachments you mentioned, we’ll align internally and confirm the 6/18 slot.

Appreciate it —

Alex —

Appreciate the follow-up questions. Short answers below and next actions. If you want more detail Rafael and I can cover any item on the 6/18 technical call.

- Retention: Our hosted offering maintains audit logs for 90 days by default. For customers requiring longer retention (12–24 months), we provide configurable retention on Redwood Dedicated or via log export integration to your SIEM (we can also retain on your behalf for 13 months as an enterprise option). We’ll outline costs in the follow-up.

- DPA & subprocessors: The attached DPA template includes our current subprocessor list in Appendix A. None of our subprocessors have access to decrypted customer content by default; keys are encrypted and KMS access is restricted. We are generally able to accept narrow, mutually agreed edits to the DPA; breach notification SLA of 48 hours is something we can discuss with legal.

- Pen test: We can provide a redacted appendix that includes affected endpoints and CVE IDs (no PII or raw logs). That will be included in the pen test summary attachment.

- CMK / Encryption: Customer-managed keys via KMS are supported on Dedicated and Private deployments today. For hosted customers we offer envelope encryption and are rolling out a CMK option for Enterprise tenants (ETA Q4 2026).
